title: Feedback Constellation: Annotary Brief and Prioritized Ask Map
body:
Purpose:
This note compiles November field feedback from 8 named accounts + 12 mid-market users into a single, lightly-structured map. Think of requests as a constellation: individual asks (stars) grouped by product gravity wells (hosted, dedicated, private, console, optimize). Goal is to surface high-leverage asks that reduce friction or materially lower TCO for production inference.

Methodology / provenance:
- Sources: 1:1s, support transcripts (last 90 days), SRE incident postmortems, and two customer workshops in Oct-Nov.
- Triage: each raw ask was tagged with the product area it most impacts and a short rationale. We then scored impact (customer pain / revenue risk) and implementation effort (rough eng estimate).
- Tone: this is a working synthesis, not a final roadmap input. Use for scoping, experiment design, and clarifying customer tradeoffs.

High-level themes (constellation overview):
1) Predictable tail latency for streaming workloads (hosted-api / dedicated) — frequent and high impact
   - Problem: Several customers report bursty prompt patterns that produce large tail latency spikes under our default batching heuristics, especially with streaming enabled.
   - Representative quote: "We get great median latency but the tails kill the user experience during heavy multi-user sessions." — Fintech POC
   - Typical asks: per-route latency SLOs, streaming-aware batching knobs, and a simulated traffic test harness in Console.

2) Cost transparency for mixed-precision / quantized variants (optimize / hosted-api) — moderate impact, low-to-medium effort
   - Problem: Customers want simple signal linking model variant -> expected per-token cost and accuracy impact for their specific prompts. They dislike relying on general benchmarks.
   - Asks: A per-model-per-precision cost estimator (console + API) that takes sample prompts and returns estimated token throughput, token cost delta, and a small accuracy delta estimate.

3) Private deployment onboarding friction (private-deployments) — high impact for enterprise deals
   - Problem: Networking and KMS integration steps are frequently the longest blocking items in POCs. Lack of a checklist and clearer rollback guidance causes delays.
   - Asks: downloadable terraform module, an automated KMS integration validator, and a pre-flight checklist in Console with clear rollback instructions.

4) KV cache visibility and debugging (serving-runtime / observability) — medium impact, low effort
   - Problem: Customers debugging context-truncation or stale-prefix issues want a way to introspect KV cache hits/misses per request without exposing sensitive content.
   - Asks: an anonymized hit/miss heatmap in Console, and an SDK option to surface cache-key metadata (hash, length) in traces.

5) Rollout safety for model switches (console-and-rollouts) — moderate impact, medium effort
   - Problem: Teams need more granular canary controls (by customer segment, token budget, or route) and better post-rollout quality guards tied to evals.
   - Asks: route-level canaries, automatic rollback on quality regression (eval trigger), and a visual diff for token-cost delta pre/post.

Prioritized asks (quick list ordered by customer pain + revenue risk):
- P1: Streaming-tail SLO policy + streaming-aware batching toggle for hosted + dedicated (multiple paying customers flagged this; blocker for productionizing chat-heavy flows).
- P1: Private preflight + terraform starter + KMS validator (directly shortens sales cycles for 3 enterprise prospects).
- P2: Per-prompt cost/accuracy estimator for quantized model variants (high product value; useful to Optimize roadmap).
- P3: KV-cache hit/miss visibility in Console + SDK trace hooks (low lift, high debugging ROI).
- P3: Route-level canary rollout controls + eval-linked rollback hook.

Concrete customer vignettes (short):
- Health-tech customer: suffered 3 production incidents where streaming responses stalled for up to 8s during peak. They requested a way to tie SLO windows to their patient-facing chat routes and to disable batching for specific routes.
- Marketplace company: wants to swap to a 4-bit quantized variant to shave per-request cost ~30% but fears hallucination increase. Asked for a tool that runs their 500-sample prompt set against both variants and shows delta in key metrics.
- Regulated financial customer: their security team blocked a private deployment because our KMS workflow required manual cert steps; they asked for terraform + automated smoke test to prove secrets/keys rotation.

Quick experiments we can run (3–6 week bets):
- Experiment A (2 weeks): Short-circuit – add a per-route "streaming-safe" flag that disables continuous batching and measure tail percentiles on 2 pilot customers.
- Experiment B (3 weeks): Cost-estimator prototype – build a serverless job where customers upload 50 representative prompts; run fast-pass inference on candidate variants and return token & quality deltas.
- Experiment C (4 weeks): KV visibility toggle – wire existing trace events to a Console panel (anonymized) and enable for ops contacts at 5 customers.

Implementation notes / engineering signals:
- Streaming-tail fixes interact with existing batch autoscaler heuristics; we should avoid naive disable-by-default approaches. Consider a tiered approach: (1) per-route toggle, (2) adaptive batching that respects route SLOs, (3) fallback to smaller batch sizes during detected tail spikes.
- Cost-estimator requires a secure sandbox to run customer prompts. We can leverage existing dedicated pools or a low-cost hosted sandbox. Need legal sign-off for short-term data retention.
- Private preflight is mainly infra work and docs + 1 small UX piece. High ROI on enterprise conversions.

Risks / open questions:
- How do we represent accuracy regressions for customers who lack labeled eval sets? (Suggest a conservative "disagreement rate" metric plus human review flows.)
- What security posture do enterprises require for running sample prompts in estimator? (Encryption-in-transit + ephemeral retention + opt-in TOS.)
- Are there cost/ops implications of exposing KV metadata to customer traces? (We should anonymize and rate-limit metadata exports.)

Suggested next steps (owner + timing):
- Customer Success (Priya) to prioritize P1 customers and schedule pilot for Experiment A (week of Nov 22).
- Product-Optimize (Lena) to scope a cost-estimator prototype with Research (Evan) and legal (TBD) within 2 weeks.
- Eng-serving-runtime (Marco) to draft an implementation approach for per-route streaming knobs and a perf-safety checklist (ETA: 3 weeks).

Appendix: quick scorecard sample (how we scored each ask)
- Impact: 1 (low) — 5 (high)
- Effort: 1 (low) — 5 (high)
- Revenue-risk weight: 1 (low) — 3 (high)

Example row (Health-tech streaming SLO): Impact=5, Effort=3, RevWeight=3 -> priority band: P1

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact. If you want a decomposed CSV of all raw asks with tags + scoring, reply to this doc and I'll attach the export.
- Please flag any missing stakeholders before we escalate P1 asks into sprint planning.

-- Priya
Customer Success
